newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Abbey raises profits, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Abbey raises profits, shares rise.

text.p: Britain's Abbey National Plc got the banking sector reporting season underway on Tuesday with a 23 percent rise in first half pre-tax profits to 687 million pounds ($1.1 billion).
After an initial fall on the results, with some traders expressing disappointement at the dividend level, Abbey shares stood four pence firmer by midmorning at 814p.
The bank said it will maintain its progressive dividend policy and announced a 17 percent increase for the first half to 10.2 pence per share -- at the lower end of market forecasts.
Analysts said the results were in line with expectations and reflected what is likely from other banks reporting over the next 10 days.
The figures showed Abbey's traditional mortgage and savings markets suffering from tight margins but its other sectors such as consumer lending doing well.
In the first half of last year, Abbey made a profit before tax of 558 million pounds and paid an 8.7 pence dividend.

Abbey chief executive Peter Birch said the bank will not now expand its life assurance and long-term savings business by acquisition, after missing out earlier this year in the auction for mutual life company Scottish Amicable.

"We missed out on ScotAm this year," Birch told Reuters. "We're growing very strongly organically and we think the cost of acquisition is very high. So we will try now to grow organically rather than by acquisition."
Birch said funds under management had grown strongly, rising by about 50 percent to over 9.0 billion pounds over the last year. "The life division is doing extraordinarily well," Birch said.

Birch said he did not rule out acquisitions in other parts of the Abbey's business, noting it had recently completed the takeover of financial services group Cater Allen to boost its treasury and offshore segments.
But he said that a repetition of Abbey's 1996 acquisition of National & Provincial building society was unlikely to be repeated because of the current high price of building society assets .
Birch agreed that, despite the disappearance of many large societies, there were still some that would be worth acquiring. "But there are a lot of people interested in them too," he said.

There has recently been a spate of rumours in the financial services sector, the latest of which puts Royal Bank of Scotland in talks with the Birmingham Midshires Building Society in a deal which would be worth 650 million pounds.

The Abbey's continuing acquisitive nature was confirmed when the bank said it will reduce its current 9.2 percent tier one capital ratio to around 7.25 percent by the end of the next three years while maintaining progressive dividends.
"We are still acquisitive and we'll continue to use capital to make acquisitions and pay our shareholders well," Birch said.

Abbey increased provisions against bad debts to 70 million pounds in the half compared to 49 million stg in the first half of last year but Birch said this was a function of good growth in unsecured lending and he remained comfortable about credit quality.
Birch admitted that margins were under pressure in the mortgage and savings market in the first half and the bank reported a net outflow of 300 million pounds of liquid savings in the first half.
Its market share of 0.6 percent of the increase of outstanding UK mortgages was well below its 14.3 percent market share of the stock.
"The market is very competitive and we've performed reasonably well but not as well as we would have liked," Birch said.
He said the market had been a false one during the first half of the year with billions of pounds of deposits locked in accounts at building societies converting to bank status.
Birch said house prices in Britain were expected to rise by around eight percent this year, slowing to five percent next year. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
